clue.text: Normal procedure at home, interrupting course

indicators.note: one piece interrupting another breaks into it, so it sits inside the other

parts.note: a route is the course taken from place to place
in means at home, as in 'staying in tonight'

explanation.surface: Someone's usual habit of being at home cuts across a planned course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is the regular, habitual way something is done, a normal procedure.

clue.text: Remember to pay another visit

explanation.surface: A reminder to go and see someone again.
explanation.definitionFit: Recall means remember, and split as re-call it means to call on someone once more.

clue.text: Abrupt changes of direction upset empty vessels

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: urns are vessels, for ashes or tea

explanation.surface: Knocked-over vessels with nothing in them cause sudden swerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the word emptied, giving UT.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-turn is a complete reversal of course, so U-turns are abrupt changes of direction.

clue.text: Going on to make entrance without expert

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the entrance word goes around the expert

parts.note: ingress is a formal word for an entrance or the act of entering
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: Getting in without help from a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in progress is under way, still going on.

clue.text: Moderates get revolutionary to swallow arsenic

indicators.note: the turned word takes in the poison's symbol, as if swallowing it
something revolutionary turns round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to get something is to see it, understand it
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: Political moderates persuade a radical to take poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' means understand here, and 'revolutionary' turns that word round before 'to swallow' takes in the poison's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate pain or tension is to lessen it, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Horses from stud mostly fed with corn mash

indicators.note: the shortened stud word is filled up with the mashed letters
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob on a surface

indicators.note: mash means the letters are crushed and remixed

explanation.surface: Horses from a breeding stud are given mashed corn as feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stud' wants to be the horse farm; it is BOSS, a knob, cut to BOS. 'mash' reworks CORN into RONC.
explanation.definitionFit: Broncos are wild or half-broken horses of the American West.

clue.text: Cook is aware of audible college

indicators.note: audible tells us the words heard spoken make the answer

parts.note: cook gives braise and is aware of gives knows

explanation.surface: A chef who knows a loud institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Brasenose is one of the colleges of Oxford University.

clue.text: Fish getting away from posh speaker?

indicators.note: an upper-class accent famously says the word for leaving as if it rhymed with dwarf

parts.note: off means getting away, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: A fish slips away from a plummy-voiced talker.
explanation.walkthrough: The plummy British drawl pronounces 'off' as 'orf', which spells the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe is a freshwater fish, a golden form of the ide kept in ponds.

clue.text: Female writing line in smart gear

parts.note: chic means smart, stylish

indicators.note: the line letter goes into the gear word

parts.note: kit is gear, equipment or clothing

explanation.surface: Women's fiction set out in fashionable clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chick lit is a genre of popular fiction written for and about young women.

clue.text: FBI agents entertained by Tess playing parts

indicators.note: guests entertained by a host are within it, so the agents go inside
playing suggests the letters are played about with

parts.note: G-men are US federal agents, the FBI's 'government men'

explanation.surface: Federal agents are hosted by an actress called Tess as she performs her roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the name into SETS before 'entertained by' wraps it round the agents; G-men is old American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Segments are sections or pieces of a whole.

clue.text: Friend beginning to play the fool

parts.note: a chum is a friend

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pal who starts to clown around.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump is a foolish, gullible person, a dolt.

clue.text: Taking supporters back with cast

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way

parts.note: fans are supporters
to fling is to cast, to throw

explanation.surface: Stealing supporters' backing with a throw, perhaps in fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To snaffle is British slang for taking something, often sneakily.

clue.text: At sea, eat no slugs as seafood

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A sailor refuses slugs and eats seafood instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Langoustes are spiny lobsters, served as shellfish.

clue.text: Boat's destination in song that sounds blue

indicators.note: what is heard is the colour word, spelt differently

parts.note: sky blue; the sky is the blue

explanation.surface: A wistful tune names where a ship is bound.
explanation.walkthrough: The Skye Boat Song runs 'Over the sea to Skye'; Skye is a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Skye Boat Song the boat carries Bonnie Prince Charlie to Skye.

clue.text: Baker's aid is secure after turning on grill

indicators.note: the secure word comes after the rearranged letters
turning the letters over rearranges them

parts.note: to pin is to secure, fasten

explanation.surface: A baker's helper fastens food on a grill after turning it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolling pin is the cylinder bakers use to flatten pastry.

clue.text: Head examiner is rating cool form

indicators.note: form means shape anew, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A chief examiner gives a cool assessment of a candidate's form.
explanation.definitionFit: A craniologist studies skulls, literally examining heads.

clue.text: Musical director finally hurried up? That's the story

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

parts.note: ran means hurried

explanation.surface: A musical director rushed on stage: that's the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical director' reads as one person but splits in two, with 'finally' taking the last letter of 'director'; 'up' turns the whole lot round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a story.

clue.text: Bird dog? A small pig!

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: Someone peers at a bird: is it a dog, or a little pig?
explanation.definitionFit: The curassow is a large turkey-like bird of tropical America.

clue.text: Restful location in which time-wasting matriarch unwound?

indicators.note: unwound means the letters are untwisted and set out afresh
wasting time means losing it, so the time letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A family matriarch idles away the hours relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking T from MATRIARCH leaves MARIARCH, which 'unwound' reworks.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a comfortable seat with arms, a place to rest.

clue.text: Fully booked in mid-June and second half of July

indicators.note: the booked word goes in between the two calendar fragments
mid picks the middle letters of the word
the second half is the last two of four letters

parts.note: reserved means booked

explanation.surface: A holiday spot is completely booked through the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fully booked' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Fully' is the definition, 'booked' the piece that goes 'in' between the fragments of the two months.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreservedly means without reservation, completely.

clue.text: Bones in back start to ache

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bones in someone's back begin to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterna is the plural of sternum, the breastbone.

clue.text: Promise to participate

definitions.meaning: to pledge or bind oneself, as in a betrothal
to take part, as in engaging in debate

explanation.surface: A pledge to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: One engages to do something by promising it, and engages in an activity by joining it.

clue.text: Month not the first that may be triumphal

indicators.note: losing the first letter of the month word

parts.note: March is a month

explanation.surface: A month that isn't January might still end in triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A triumphal arch is a monumental gateway celebrating a victory.

clue.text: Unnecessary words? Not about bear

parts.note: padding is wordy filler in writing

indicators.note: about means turned round, read backwards

explanation.surface: Rejecting waffle, someone refuses to discuss bears.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington Bear is the marmalade-loving bear from London children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is a famous fictional bear named after a London railway station.

clue.text: Live comfortably after introduction to duchess

indicators.note: the comfortable word comes after the duchess's first letter
the introduction to a word is its first letter

parts.note: well means comfortably, as in living well

explanation.surface: A duchess, once introduced to society, lives in comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live in a place, reside.

clue.text: Cheese for entrées that's also for starters

indicators.note: the starters of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A cheese suitable for main courses also works as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrées' means main courses in the US but starters in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a crumbly white Greek cheese of sheep or goat milk.

clue.text: Team, say, leading in America

indicators.note: the say word leads, coming in front of the team word

parts.note: to state is to say
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team, so to speak, ahead in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateside is an adverb meaning in or to the United States.

clue.text: Grand filling for soldier's jacket

indicators.note: the grand letter fills the inside of the soldier word

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier; the possessive ties him to the jacket
a grand is a thousand, abbreviated K

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds for a soldier's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket.

clue.text: Pottery broken by remote conflict

indicators.note: the pottery word is broken open by the remote word put inside

parts.note: ware is pottery, as in earthenware
far means remote, distant

explanation.surface: Crockery smashed by long-range fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare is armed conflict between forces.

clue.text: A king involved in The French Connection

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit in the French article

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A monarch is cast in the film The French Connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkage is a link or connection between things.
